annotation.title_clean: Sentry robots in action: ethical and legal issues of automated weapon in South Korea
annotation.title_en: Sentry robots in action: ethical and legal issues of automated weapon in South Korea
annotation.venue: ICRES 2022: 7th International Conference on Robot Ethics and Standards
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper examining South Korea's SGR-A1 sentry robot deployed at the DMZ and the ethical and legal issues of lethal autonomous weapons. It reviews Korean AI and robot ethics charters and the Intelligent Robots Act, and argues for AI-risk management, a legal responsibility framework and trustworthiness-based governance.
key_provisions_or_claims: SGR-A1 sentry robot at the DMZ raises concerns about autonomous killing and civilian casualties.
LAWS create accountability gaps and lower the threshold for war.
South Korea has not endorsed a ban on fully autonomous weapons.
Korean ethics charters stress human control and bar AI from being used to injure or kill.
Calls for a national AI governance system built on lawful, ethical and robust trustworthiness.
